identity.title: ALMA and VLA measurements of frequency-dependent time lags in Sagittarius A*: evidence for a relativistic outflow

paper_type_evidence.quote: To summarize, we have measured time lags in Sgr A* light curves from 100 GHz to 19 GHz using ALMA and the VLA.

evidence.quote: Located at a distance of 8.3$\pm 0.4$ kpc from the solar system, its mass is calculated to be $4.3\pm 0.4\cdot 10^6$ $M_{\odot}$

question.value: Do Sgr A* light curves at 19-100 GHz show frequency-dependent time lags indicating an expanding, relativistic outflow/jet?

evidence.quote: Presence of a jet implies that specific correlations should be detected between light curves at different frequencies.
observations were made in ALMA cycle 0 on May 18, 2012 from 03:30:47 UT to 10:52:16 UT (project code: 2011.0.00887.S)

bands.value: ALMA bands 3, 6, 7 observed; only ~100 GHz (Band 3) used here

evidence.quote: In this paper we limit discussion to the 100 GHz ALMA data

evidence.quote: Each pair of spectral windows covered 3.75 GHz bandwidth for a total of 7.5 GHz bandwidth per ALMA band.

evidence.quote: at random, half of the data points (20 out of 40) for a given VLA light curve were dropped before attempting a fit with the FRED function. For each light curve, this was iterated 500 times.

findings_qualitative.value: Higher-frequency light curves peak earlier than lower-frequency ones (25 GHz an exception)

evidence.quote: With the 25 GHz data as notable exception, the maxima occur at later times for the lower observing frequencies

claims.hypothesis: Sgr A* light curves show frequency-dependent time lags consistent with an outflow
claims.experiment: FRED fits to VLA and ALMA 100 GHz light curves from one track
claims.result: Maxima shift later with decreasing frequency from 100 to 19 GHz
claims.finding: Time lags exist, with a moderately relativistic directed outflow

evidence.quote: Higher-frequency light curves are seen to have their maxima at earlier times than the lower-frequency light curves.

claims.hypothesis: Lags are consistent with earlier reports
claims.experiment: Compare linear lag/wavelength fit with Yusef-Zadeh et al.

evidence.quote: they are compatible

claims.hypothesis: Short-term fluctuations share the lag of the long-term trend
claims.finding: Short-term variations are likely calibration residuals

evidence.quote: This cross-correlation peaks at zero time lag, suggesting that the short-term fluctuations have a different origin from the long-term trends.

why_this_method.value: FRED fitting chosen because ZDCF is dominated by zero-lag spikes

evidence.quote: we chose the simple and robust approach of fitting the longer-term flux density evolution in all light curves

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: ZDCF rejected for lag estimates due to zero-lag peaks

evidence.quote: the zero-lag peaks preclude any meaningful time lag estimates to be made this way

limitations_admitted.value: Results from a single track; ALMA cadence coarse

evidence.quote: As these results are based upon measurements of a light-curve feature from a single track

referee_caveats_inferred: Single ALMA peak with 15-min cadence may not be causally linked to VLA maxima
25 GHz outlier and coherence loss at low elevation weaken the lag trend
Velocity depends on assumed quiescent size-frequency relation and geometry
